comments.author: @larrylezon1590
comments.text: Consumerism is so pervasive and results in a lot of the debt people have.  The dopamine dump people get when they receive a package from Amazon or buy something from a store that they don't truly need is addictive.  People need to recognize this and get a grasp on it.  I grew up in the '70's - Dad always turning the lights off, lines for gas, reheated leftover macaroni and cheese for dinner, etc.  I worked 3 jobs in HS, and 2 for most of my adult life.  I was able to retire at 50yo, I have a nice house - not a mansion, but enough for the family, multiple vehicles, and no concerns about paying my bills.  I cannot grasp how so many people are in such dire financial conditions.  I've had my struggles and no one has given me a handout.  Hard work, determination, and cutting corners are the keys to success.  Stop buying stuff you don't actually NEED.  Turn the heat or A/C up or down a couple of degrees.  Turn off the extra lights and unplug chargers when not in use.  Buy a used car that gets good gas mileage.  Shop for groceries at cheaper stores like Aldi.  Stop ordering out and using Door Dash.  Don't buy a new cell phone until your current one is just about unusable.  No one who truly likes you cares about the car you drive, the phone you use, your newest hairstyle, your manicure, etc.  Shop at Goodwill or similar stores for your clothes and home goods.  Plant a garden and grow your own food basics - tomatoes, onions, potatoes, peppers - it's almost effortless, but every penny saved counts.
